flood.value: Harris County Floodplain Management Regulations (amended/effective 2019-07-09; post-Harvey rule from 2018): new homes in the 1% (100-yr) or 0.2% (500-yr, zone X-shaded) floodplain need lowest finished floor (top of subfloor) >= 24 in above the 0.2% flood elevation or 12 in above the nearest public street crown, whichever is higher; 36 in in a floodway reported. In the 100-yr floodplain no fill for elevation (piers/stem walls). Outside the floodplain: Class I permit; inside: Class II. If lowest adjacent grade >= BFE, processed as outside 100-yr.

source.title: Regulations of Harris County, Texas for Floodplain Management (amended/effective 9 July 2019)

plainLanguage: Cypress is unincorporated Harris County, so there is no city zoning and no city building permit. You still need a Harris County Engineering residential development permit, which checks flooding and drainage. If your lot is in the 100- or 500-year floodplain, the floor must sit at least 2 ft above the 500-year flood level, or 1 ft above the street crown, whichever is higher, and you cannot use fill to get there. Your setbacks, masonry and design rules come from the plat and your HOA deed restrictions. Water and sewer come from a MUD, which sets its own tap fees and a property tax. Cypress is not in the coastal windstorm area. Plan on an engineer-designed slab.
